out.rationale: Hammond and Adam-Day list not evaluating simultaneous versus sequential debate as a limitation of their own protocols, which they evaluate on only two domains, with a graph isomorphism task and a code-validation task. Sudhir et al. report no significant effect from switching between simultaneous and sequential debate or changing turn count, with a gpt-4o-mini judge on GSM8K, so the gap and the result concern different tasks; Hammond and Adam-Day train their agents, while the passage does not say whether Sudhir et al.'s debaters are trained.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether simultaneous versus sequential debate matters, for LLM debate on GSM8K

out.rationale: Kenton et al. report that changes to the setup (number of turns, best-of-N sampling, few-shot, chain-of-thought) seem to have little effect on results. Sudhir et al. report no significant effect of changing the number of turns or switching between simultaneous and sequential debate; the passages do not show whether the two papers share agents, judges, tasks or metric.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: whether the number of debate turns matters for debate results
